record.paper_title: A Short Note on some open problems in the geometry of operator ideals
record.original_question: Let (A, A) be a maximal Banach ideal. Are the following two conditions equivalent: first, that (A, A) is right-accessible, meaning that for every finite-dimensional Banach space E, every Banach space Y, every operator T in L(E, Y), and every epsilon > 0, there exist a finite-dimensional subspace N of Y and an operator S in L(E, N) with T = J_N^Y S and A(S) <= (1 + epsilon) A(T); and second, that (A, A) satisfies the A-local reflexivity principle described in Definition 1.1?

evidence.quote: (B, B) is called right-accessible, if for any two Banach spaces E and Y , dim(E) < ∞, any operator T ∈ L(E, Y ) and any ε > 0 there are a finite dimensional subspace N of Y and S ∈ L(E, N) such that T = JYN S and B(S) ≤ (1 + ε)B(T).
Proposition 1.4 (cf. [13]) If (A, A) is a right-accessible maximal Banach ideal, then the A-LRP holds. We still do not know whether the statement in Proposition 1.4 can be reversed.
Problem 1.5 Let (A, A) be a maximal Banach ideal. Are then the following statements equivalent? (i) (A, A) is right-accessible. (ii) (A, A) satisfies the A-LRP.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathfrak{L}$ denote the class of all bounded linear operators between Banach spaces. A Banach operator ideal is a pair $(\mathfrak{A}, A)$ where $\mathfrak{A}\subseteq\mathfrak{L}$ is a two-sided ideal and $A:\mathfrak{A}\to[0,\infty)$ is an ideal-norm making each component $\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$ a Banach space and satisfying the usual ideal axioms (containing finite-rank operators with $A(x'\otimes y)=\|x'\|\|y\|$, and $A(RTS)\le \|R\|A(T)\|S\|$). The ideal $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is called maximal if for every operator $T\in\mathfrak{L}(X,Y)$,
$$A(T)=\sup\{A(Q^Y_F\, T\, J^X_M)\,:\, M\subseteq X\text{ finite-dimensional},\ F\subseteq Y\text{ finite-codimensional closed}\},$$
where $J^X_M:M\hookrightarrow X$ is the inclusion and $Q^Y_F:Y\to Y/F$ is the quotient map, with the convention that $T\in\mathfrak{A}$ iff this supremum is finite.

For a closed subspace $N\subseteq Y$ let $J^Y_N:N\hookrightarrow Y$ denote the inclusion. The ideal $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is right-accessible if for every finite-dimensional Banach space $E$, every Banach space $Y$, every $T\in\mathfrak{L}(E,Y)$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a finite-dimensional subspace $N\subseteq Y$ and $S\in\mathfrak{L}(E,N)$ with $T=J^Y_N S$ and $A(S)\le(1+\varepsilon)A(T)$.

For an operator ideal $(\mathfrak{A},A)$, one says that $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ satisfies the A-local reflexivity principle (A-LRP) if for every Banach space $X$, every Banach space $Y$, every finite-dimensional subspace $M\subseteq X^{**}$, every finite-dimensional subspace $F\subseteq Y^*$, every operator $T\in\mathfrak{A}(X^{**},Y)$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists an operator $\tilde T\in\mathfrak{A}(X,Y)$ such that
(i) $\langle \tilde T x, y^*\rangle = \langle T x, y^*\rangle$ for all $x\in X$, $y^*\in F$,
(ii) $\langle \tilde T^{**} m, y^*\rangle = \langle T m, y^*\rangle$ for all $m\in M$, $y^*\in F$, and
(iii) $A(\tilde T)\le (1+\varepsilon)\,A(T)$.

Question. Let $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ be a maximal Banach ideal. Are the following two statements equivalent?
(i) $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ is right-accessible.
(ii) $(\mathfrak{A},A)$ satisfies the A-local reflexivity principle.

It is known that (i) implies (ii). Determine whether (ii) implies (i).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published proof or disproof of the converse implication (A-LRP implies right-accessibility) for maximal Banach ideals. The forward direction (right-accessibility implies A-LRP) is established in the literature on accessibility of operator ideals (e.g., Oertel's work), but the equivalence question appears not to have a confirmed resolution in available sources.

status_evidence.title: Extension of Finite Rank Operators and Operator Ideals with the Property (I)
status_evidence.snippet: Each right-accessible maximal Banach ideal (A, A) even satisfies such a principle of local reflexivity for operator ideals.
status_evidence.claim: The forward implication (right-accessibility implies A-LRP) is known.

status_evidence.title: On normed products of operator ideals which contain L2 as a factor
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses accessibility properties of maximal Banach ideals and Pisier's counterexamples but does not establish the converse implication.
status_evidence.claim: No confirmed proof of the converse implication appears in standard references on accessibility of maximal Banach ideals.
